extracted.intended_audience: Patent proprietors, in-house counsel, and practitioners handling pharmaceutical or plant protection product patents in Europe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility and basic requirements for obtaining a Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) in Europe/Denmark, including the necessary patent and regulatory-approval conditions and relevant legal considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum extension term
rubrics_metrics.description: For some patents, it is possible to obtain an extension of the patent protection for up to 5 years via an application for a Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPCs can extend the effective patent term by up to five years to compensate for regulatory approval delays. This is the statutory maximum extension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: applicable product types and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: This extension applies to patents protecting pharmaceutical or plant protection products in Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPCs are limited in subject-matter (medicinal/pharmaceutical products and plant protection products) and are a European/Member State mechanism — eligibility depends on European and national rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: proprietor of a granted patent protecting the product
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be the proprietor of a granted patent protecting the product in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent must be granted (not merely applied for) and must effectively protect the specific product for which the SPC is sought—i.e., the product falls within the scope/claims of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement: granted marketing approval for the product
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have a granted marketing approval for that product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid marketing authorization/approval is required (national or EU as applicable). The timing and nature of the MA are decisive for SPC entitlement and term calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of SPC legislation and case law
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and prosecution should take into account SPC case law in Denmark and the European SPC legislation in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and scope issues are shaped by evolving national and EU case law and statutory interpretation; practical filing/prosecution requires attention to jurisdictional nuances, precedent, and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit constraint: not all patents are eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Only 'some patents' are eligible for an SPC—eligibility is constrained by product type, patent coverage, and regulatory approval status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before pursuing an SPC, confirm that the patent claims cover the marketed product and that the regulatory approval qualifies for SPC purposes; eligibility assessments are case-specific.
